Testimony on behalf of Maine Equal Justice in support of LD 85 An Act to Revitalize the
Maine Temporary Assistance for Needy Families Advisory Council
_ February 5, 2025
Good afternoon Senator lngwersen, Representative Meyer, and Members of the Committee on Health and Human Services. My name is Ann Danforth and I use she/her
pronouns. |'m a Senior Policy Advocate at Maine Equal Justice (MEJ), a nonprofit civil legal aid provider working to increase economic security, opportunity, and equity for people in Maine.
l'm here today to testify in strong support of LD 85, An Act to Revitalize the Maine
Temporary Assistance for Needy Families Advisory Council.
Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TAN F) and its employment and training program, ASPIRE, are key social infrastructure and workforce support programs in our state. TANF/ASPIRE provides critical support for families with children, enabling them to make ends meet. it also provides parents with the opportunity to pursue education and training that can help lift families out of poverty, and at the same time, strengthen our
state's workforce.
Maine Equal Justice has worked to improve the TANF program in Maine since its inception in 1996. Over the years, we have worked to help pass legislation that creates more opportunities and pathways out of poverty for TANF participants, including by
helping to create the Parents as Scholars (PaS) and Higher Opportunity for Pathways to
Employment (HOPE) programs; increasing the TANF benefit amount; reducing the
"benefits cliff"; enhancing transitional support services; creating more robust outcomes metrics related to TANF/ASPIRE that are now reported on through the LIFT report delivered to this committee; and more.

Through our organizing work with MEJ's TANF/ASPIRE Leadership Team members -- a
group of single moms who have participated in TANF and work with MEJ to inform and advocate for our policy priorities -- we know well that the most important voices in how
TANF functions are those of participants. We also know how important it is to
compensate people with lived experience for the time and the expertise they bring. Too often, the people bringing the most lived experience to an advisory council, taskforce, or commission are the only people at the table not being compensated for their time there since everyone else is participating as part of theirjob. Their experience is essential to
fully understand the way programs work for the people who they are meant to serve so we should be compensating them for that expertise.
LD 85 would authorize reimbursement and compensation for TANF Advisory Council members with lived experience. This would make it more likely that TANF parents will
be able to participate given their financial and time constraints. It also sends an
important signal that we value and need their input.
We believe it is long overdue to revitalize the TANF Advisory Council. We hope this
revitalized Council will be a place where members can weigh in on important issues related to TANF/ASPIRE -- including how participants feel they are being treated and supported by Fedcap in meeting their career and individual goals; how TANF/ASPIRE can be further strengthened to better meet the needs of families and our state's workforce; and how TANF funds are being prioritized and spent in Maine.
Thank you for your time and l'm happy to answer any questions you may have.
Ann Danforth

Testimony of the Office for Family Independence
Maine Department of Health and Human Services
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services
In support of LD 85,
An Act to Revitalize the Maine Temporary Assistance for Needy Families Advisory Council
Sponsor: Representative Meyer Hearing Date: February 5, 2025
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Health and Human Services, my name is Ian Yaffe, and I serve as the Director of the Office for Family Independence (OFI) in the Maine Department of Health and Human Services. I am here today to testify in support of LD 85, An Act to Revitalize the Maine Temporary Assistance for
Needy Families Advisory Council.
I'd first like to say thank you to Chair Meyer for bringing forth this bill on behalf of the
Department. The TANF Advisory Council is authorized by 22 MRSA �3789-D, which outlines
the duties and the membership. Throughout the years since its fonnation, the Advisory Council has varied in its viability and effectiveness. Especially since the pandemic, participation in the Council has been lackluster. It has been kept alive through the efforts of Jean Dempster, a
faithful member. We greatly appreciate her work. Ms. Dempster has now retired from her role at New Ventures, Maine, and we are seeking to revitalize the Council. My office has undertaken
an effort to do so, conducting a listening session and an open forum to generate interest and
attract new members. We have also arranged for administrative support for the Council and solicited nominations for the Council seats. We received a robust slate of nominations from
community partners and stakeholders. These are currently under review, and we anticipate the appointment of new members in the coming weeks.
In conjunction with those efforts, this legislation will simplify the Council's structure and
increase its effectiveness. Among other provisions, it authorizes compensation, similar to the
legislative per diem, for Council members that are not otherwise compensated for their time serving. The Council is designed to bring a diverse array of perspectives and experiences together, and the compensation provision will further that mission, especially to bring more
voices with lived experience in the TANF program to the table. The costs associated with this
proposal can be absorbed into existing budgets, and so this bill does not require additional
appropriations.
We believe that a vibrant Advisory Council, which includes varied perspectives, will only serve to benefit the TANF and ASPIRE programs and those that participate in those programs. We

support this proposed legislation and appreciate your consideration.
Thank you for your time and attention. I would be happy to answer any questions you may have and to make myself available for questions at the work session.

Testimony of House Chair Rep. Michele Meyer presenting
LD 85, An Act to Revitalize the Maine Temporary Assistance for
Needy Families Advisory Council
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services
Senator Ingwersen and fellow members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services, I am Representative Michele Meyer, representing House District 150, which includes
Eliot and parts of Kittery and South Berwick. I am glad to be before you to present LD 85, An
Act to Revitalize the Maine Temporary Assistance for Needy Families Advisory Council.

The Department is seeking to renew and revitalize the Council that is designed to bring together a vibrant array of perspectives to discuss and then advise the Department on issues affecting
recipients of Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, or TANF. This can include education,
training, job opportunities, quality employment and business ownership opportunities, the operation of any postsecondary education programs, and other matters. Discussions among groups with varying, but related, lived experiences are critical to improving programs that
support our most vulnerable populations. This is why I was glad to submit this legislation on
behalf of the Department.

The bill adjusts the membership of the Council to better reflect its statutory charge, and it

I

authorizes compensation for members. As we all know, serving on committees, councils,

working groups, and task forces is time consuming and can take time away from our full-time

jobs. I believe those who are willing to designate their time to share their experiences to better

others deserve to be compensated for that time.

These changes will help to support the functionality and effectiveness of both the TANF and
ASPIRE program, and I hope that you'll join me in supporting this initiative. The Department will follow my testimony to further explain this proposal and take any questions you may have.
